quote.quote: Meeting of the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee was convened to discuss the effectiveness and safety of tafenoquine for the radical cure (prevention of relapse) of *P. vivax* malaria in patients 16 years and older.
An Advisory Committee meeting was held on July 12th, 2018 to discuss NDA 210795.

recommendation.text: The committee voted that the applicant provided substantial evidence of effectiveness (13:0) and safety (12:1).

quote.quote: The committee voted that the applicant provided substantial evidence of effectiveness (voted 13:0) and safety (voted 12:1) based on the data presented.

linkages.concern: A speaker at the advisory committee's open public hearing questioned the potential neurotoxic effects of tafenoquine (TQ) and the need for additional nonclinical studies, based on published neurotoxicity of other 8-aminoquinolines.
linkages.change: The approval included a postmarketing requirement (PMR 3436-1) to conduct an active pharmacovigilance surveillance study specifically soliciting for neuropsychiatric adverse reactions (along with hypersensitivity and hematologic reactions).

concern_quote.quote: During the July 12, 2018, Advisory Committee, one of the speakers at the open public hearing raised a question regarding the potential neurotoxic effects of TQ and need for additional nonclinical studies.

change_quote.quote: The approval of NDA 210795 will include a postmarketing requirement to conduct an active pharmacovigilance surveillance study to specifically solicit for neuropsychiatric adverse reactions, as well as hypersensitivity and hematological adverse reactions.

summary: An Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee (AMDAC) meeting was convened on July 12, 2018 to discuss KRINTAFEL (tafenoquine) for the radical cure of P. vivax malaria in patients 16 years and older; the committee voted 13:0 that effectiveness was demonstrated and 12:1 that safety was demonstrated. During the open public hearing, a speaker raised a concern about the potential neurotoxicity of tafenoquine and the need for additional nonclinical studies; the FDA ultimately concluded no additional animal studies were warranted but imposed a postmarketing requirement (PMR 3436-1) for an active pharmacovigilance study specifically soliciting neuropsychiatric adverse reactions. The AdComm was supportive of approval, and its principal documented influence on the application was this neuropsychiatric-focused pharmacovigilance PMR.
